Silver yarn

The silver is in the yarn, not on the fabric.

SILVAR is a men's golf apparel brand built on silver yarn. The silver is part of the thread itself, not a finish added to the cloth at the end. You will not see it, feel it, or wash it out.

The technology

The part you cannot see.

Where the silver actually goes, and what we chose to leave off the shirt. Open either of the two below.

01The fibre+

This is decided at the spinning mill rather than at the finishing plant, which is the reason it holds. Every metre of cloth carries the same amount, so a shirt cut from the end of a roll behaves like one cut from the start.

Where
At the spinning mill, before there is any cloth to treat
Consistency
Even across the roll, first metre to last
Cost
It adds no weight, no stiffness and no step to how you wash it
02What we left off+

Most of the work here is subtraction. No logo panel across the chest, no contrast piping, no reflective trim, nothing that reads as equipment. When the work is done inside the yarn, the outside is free to be plain.

Mark
Sleeve and back neck, tonal, at a size you have to look for
Hardware
Matte, chosen so it does not catch the light
Result
Nothing on it tells a room where you spent the morning

Worn

FAQ

Questions? We have answers.

What is silver yarn?+

It is yarn made with silver already in it. The silver is added at the spinning stage, so it sits inside the thread rather than in a layer on top of finished cloth. In practice that means there is nothing to rub off, nothing to re-apply, and no difference in how the garment looks, weighs or feels.

Does the silver wash out?+

No. Treatments sit on top of the cloth, which is why a treated shirt performs best the week you buy it and less well every wash after. Here there is no layer to lose.

Is SILVAR only for golf?+

It is designed for golf and cut so it does not look like golf apparel. The polo is meant to go from the first tee to lunch, to the office on a Friday, and out in the evening without reading as sportswear in any of those rooms. There is no logo across the chest and nothing technical about the way it looks.

What does SILVAR make?+

Two pieces at launch, both knitted with silver yarn: a polo and a low-cut sock. The range stays small on purpose, and each piece is built to be kept rather than replaced every season. First delivery is spring 2027.

How do I care for my SILVAR pieces?+

Machine wash cold and tumble dry low. No special detergent, no hand washing, no line drying. Avoid bleach and fabric softener, which coat fibres and reduce breathability in any performance cloth.

The company

A golf brand built by people who have made this product for other people for thirty years.

SILVAR was started by three people who spent their careers inside the apparel business, on the manufacturing side and on the selling side. Thirty years of making this exact product for other people's labels teaches you where the corners get cut, and how long a shirt really lasts once it leaves the box.

It also teaches you what golfers keep asking for and not getting: a shirt that performs without announcing it, and still looks right at a table afterwards.

So the brief was narrow on purpose. A short range, made to one standard, with silver-ion technology worked into the fabric rather than sprayed on at the end, so each piece can do its job quietly and still hang the way good clothing should.

The first pieces go to a small number of private clubs, resorts and green grass shops before they go anywhere else. Those are the people who will tell us the truth about the fit, and the people whose members notice a collar that has given up by the ninth. Trust is easier to earn there than to buy anywhere else.

Mockup notes, not part of the page
  1. Reviews are sample copy and carry no schema on purpose. The row scrolls horizontally, so on a wide screen the sixth card sits off-frame by design. They are marked on the page. Nothing here ships until there are real customers, and the structured data deliberately omits Review and AggregateRating. Marking up invented reviews is against Google's policy and, since 2024, the FTC's rule on fake reviews carries real penalties.
  2. A repetition pass ran over the whole page. The hero was explaining the technology that the next section explains, Silver Yarn and Technology opened with the same argument, and the FAQ repeated the Silver Yarn copy close to word for word. Every section now owns its own vocabulary: the hero sets the standard, Silver Yarn makes the claim and names the benefits, the product blocks carry the specs, Technology explains the mechanism, and the FAQ answers in a customer's words rather than the brand's.
  3. Technology went from four panels to two. The cloth and the wear panels only had the cotton blend and the care instructions in them, which already live on the product block and in the FAQ. Four panels was padding, and the padding is what repeated.
  4. Silver Yarn and Technology were saying the same thing. Both opened with a version of "a finish sits on the surface, a fibre does not", and the fibre panel repeated it a third time. Silver Yarn is now the claim and the three benefits; Technology is the only place the mechanism is explained, and both diagrams moved there. The "How it works" link jumps between them.
  5. The two diagrams in Silver Yarn are drawn for SILVAR, not taken from Sam's reference images. Those references belong to another brand, carry that brand's labels and fibre names (TENCEL, Modal, Polyester), and one of them shows a bomber jacket, none of which we can publish. These are schematic and not to scale; the fibre cross-section is illustrative until the mill confirms how the silver is carried.
  6. The macro cloth shot is upscaled from a small source. It is soft at full width and needs a real macro frame before launch.
  7. Freshness wording still needs the mill. The section says silver helps the fabric stay fresher between washes and stops there. Any stronger odour or antimicrobial wording needs the EPA registration number and approved language first.
  8. FAQ is trimmed to five. Sizing and the club and pro shop question moved off the homepage; both belong on their own pages, and the structured data was cut to match what is visible.
  9. Sam's seven changes are in. Banner shortened to roughly half the previous height, technology is now a collapsible accordion, "Where the price shows up" is gone, the club portal is gone, polo and sock are stacked rather than side by side with the polo leading and carrying real detail, and the company section at the bottom is rewritten and expanded.
  10. Fibre wording follows the hangtags. Premium cotton blend, as written in the trim deck. Worth knowing that it sits oddly beside the silver-ion story, and one line of confirmation from the factory would settle it either way.
  11. Chest monogram. Two of the photographs show a monogram on the chest, which Sam ruled out in favour of sleeve and back only. Kept here because they are the strongest shots; they need regenerating before launch.
  12. Socks are the trim deck design. Low-cut with the heel tab, crossed sole band and blocked toe and heel. The crew socks in the photography are a different product.
  13. Descriptor. Premium Apparel, Premium Menswear, Premium Apparel & Accessories and Menswear Essentials are all in circulation across the decks. One needs to be chosen.
